`nft.jsonl` is generated by `tools/generate_nft_fixtures.py` against mmx-node
`ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. The oracle extracts the original
Node::get_plot_nft_target, Node::call_contract and the NFT reward-field checks
from Node::validate(Block). Only class qualifiers change; contract lookups and
the current peak height come from a synthetic ledger snapshot. VM execution,
compilation, storage, VNX conversion and address parsing use the linked native
libraries. Reference sources and databases are untouched.

185 target rows include the compiled original `src/contract/plot_nft.js` at
heights 8, 9, 10, 11, 255, 256 and 257, with unlocked, permanently locked and
height-256 unlock states. They vary null, nonzero and zero farmer accounts,
method const/public/init flags, missing/wrong-type contracts and binaries,
missing methods, malformed bytecode, gas boundaries and unavailable RCALL/CREAD.
Contract metadata read costs do not consume gas in this native path.
All cases compare the repeated executable/binary lookup order; injected failures
at each lookup exercise the native resolver's exception boundary.

Return cases compare native vm::read(...).to<addr_t>() on nulls, booleans,
small/large integers (including a valid Bech32m hexadecimal-integer witness),
valid/invalid/non-UTF-8 address strings, short/long binary lists, temporary
arrays/maps, stored arrays and stored-map errors. Stored array
tails beyond byte 32 are still converted and can reject the call. Mutating
methods and SEND/MINT calls confirm that temporary state and transfers are
discarded. Null user/transaction-ID externals are checked explicitly.

27 block rows reuse signed block envelopes from `work.jsonl`. The original
reward checks validate matching/missing/incorrect NFT contracts, mismatched
resolved targets, omitted rewards, OG proofs and fallback targets. The NFT is
locked until the candidate height, exposing the native use of the *parent*
ledger height. These tests authenticate header envelopes and prepare empty
bodies; their replacement NFT proofs test shape only, with full space work
remaining covered separately by the space/VDF fixtures.

Rows share parameters, contracts, VM cells/entries and balances through named
`seed` snapshots. Rust compares targets or rejection, exact block reward-field
errors, and verifies that calls and rejected/aborted preparations publish no
writes, balances or transfers. The C++ exception text includes diagnostics that
the Rust VM does not reproduce verbatim; target acceptance and conversion must
match.
